note: Section 13: copy-cost microbenchmark, SmolLM2-135M, real GTX 1650 Vulkan, ctx=2048, 10 repetitions per region/direction (membrane-kv-tiering-copy-microbench). Uses plain (non-pinned) host malloc/vector buffers -- see prefetch_feasibility.json for why this matters.

findings.get_slower_and_noisier_than_set: GPU->host (get) is consistently slower than host->GPU (set) at every region size, and has 5-10x higher relative stddev -- e.g. all_layers_kv: get stddev=9.92ms (13% of mean) vs set stddev=1.62ms (4.7% of mean). Read-back appears to carry a real synchronization/stall cost beyond raw transfer time that write does not.
findings.effective_bandwidth_far_below_pcie_theor: 0.6-1.4 GB/s effective, well under typical PCIe x4/x8 theoretical bandwidth (multiple GB/s) -- consistent with architecture.json's async-transfer finding: plain malloc'd (non-pinned) host memory forces ggml_backend_tensor_get/set onto Vulkan's staging/synchronous path rather than a fast pinned-memory DMA path.
findings.cost_scales_with_n_tensors_not_just_byte: several_layers_kv (8 tensors, 6.29 MB) takes proportionally MORE time per byte than all_layers_kv (60 tensors, 47.19 MB) would if cost were purely bandwidth-bound (8.70ms for 6.29MB vs 75.41ms for 47.19MB implies the smaller region is markedly less bandwidth-efficient) -- per-call/per-tensor overhead (one ggml_backend_tensor_get/set call per tensor, not one batched call for the whole region) is a real, disclosed cost driver, not just raw bytes moved.
